items.title: The tame symbol is well defined independently of the factorizations and of the chosen extension
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section on the tame symbol
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes that the displayed formula for the tame symbol gives a well-defined element of kappa(m)*, i.e. that the right-hand side is independent both of the local factorizations chosen and of the admissible extension B (statement lines 831-834). The two independence statements are proved by genuinely different arguments: the first turns the two factorizations into a unit identity by clearing powers and then settles the sign through a parity check on the exponents, while the second builds a third extension C dominating both, invokes transitivity of norms, and reduces everything to the numerical identity lambda^m = prod Norm(lambda)^{m_k}, which is then verified by comparing lengths using the comparison lemma and the pushdown lemma (proof lines 838-898). What is not routine is the bookkeeping that makes lambda^m match the product of the norms, in particular the identity m = sum m_k [kappa_k : kappa]. The claim is H2.
